docs.title: DTLS
docs.text: DTLS (Datagram Transport Layer Security) extends TLS to UDP-based applications while maintaining encryption and integrity protection.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• UDP support
  • TLS-based security
  • Packet loss tolerance
  • Replay protection
  • Low-latency encryption

docs.title: Common Use Cases
docs.text:
VoIPWebRTCIoTVPNs

Secure SIP and RTP communications.

Browser real-time communications.

Lightweight secure UDP traffic.

DTLS-based VPN tunnels.

docs.title: DTLS Architecture
docs.text:
graph LR
    A[Client] --> B[UDP Network]
    B --> C[DTLS Server]

docs.title: Topics Covered
docs.text:
• OpenSSL DTLS
  • DTLS handshakes
  • UDP encryption
  • Replay protection
  • Packet loss handling
  • DTLS troubleshooting

docs.title: Example DTLS Server
docs.text: openssl s_server -dtls -accept 4444 -cert cert.pem -key key.pem

docs.title: Example DTLS Client
docs.text:
openssl s_client -dtls -connect 127.0.0.1:4444

Note

DTLS is specifically designed to handle unreliable UDP transport.

docs.title: IPsec
docs.text: IPsec (Internet Protocol Security) is a Layer 3 security framework providing encryption, integrity, and authentication for IP traffic.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Component Purpose AH Authentication ESP Encryption IKE Key exchange SA Security Association

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
Transport ModeTunnel Mode

Encrypts the payload only.

Encrypts the full IP packet.

docs.title: Common Use Cases
docs.text:
• Site-to-site VPNs
  • Enterprise WAN security
  • Secure datacenter interconnects
  • Remote-access VPNs

docs.text:
graph LR
    A[LAN A] --> B[IPsec Gateway]
    B --> C[Encrypted Tunnel]

docs.title: Topics Covered
docs.text:

docs.title: Example strongSwan Service
docs.text:
sudo systemctl restart strongswan
sudo ip xfrm state

Note

ESP is significantly more common than AH in modern deployments.

docs.title: MACsec
docs.text: MACsec (Media Access Control Security) is a Layer 2 encryption protocol defined by IEEE 802.1AE. It provides hop-by-hop confidentiality, integrity, and replay protection for Ethernet traffic.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Layer 2 encryption
  • AES-GCM confidentiality
  • Integrity protection
  • Replay attack prevention
  • Secure VLAN transport
  • Hardware acceleration support

docs.title: Typical Use Cases
docs.text:
DatacenterService ProviderEnterpriseLab Environments

Secure leaf-spine links inside datacenters.

Protect metro Ethernet and backbone links.

Secure switch-to-switch uplinks.

Validate encrypted VLAN transport.

docs.title: MACsec Architecture
docs.text:
graph LR
    A[Host A] --> B[Switch 1]
    B --> C[Encrypted Ethernet Link]
    C --> D[Switch 2]
    D --> E[Host B]

docs.title: Topics Covered
docs.text:
• SR Linux MACsec configuration
  • MKA operation
  • CAK/CKN usage
  • VLAN encryption modes
  • WAN vs LAN MACsec
  • Containerlab integration
  • Troubleshooting workflows

docs.title: Verification Commands
docs.text:
show system security macsec connectivity-association
show system security macsec interfaces

Note

MACsec encrypts Ethernet frames directly and operates independently of IP routing.

docs.title: SSH
docs.text: SSH (Secure Shell) is a secure remote access and tunnelling protocol widely used for Linux administration, automation, and secure transport.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Encrypted remote access
  • Public key authentication
  • Secure file transfer
  • Port forwarding
  • Tunnelling support

docs.title: Common SSH Services
docs.text: Service Purpose SSH Remote shell SCP Secure copy SFTP Secure file transfer SSH Tunnel Encrypted forwarding

docs.title: SSH Architecture
docs.text:
graph LR
    A[SSH Client] --> B[Encrypted Session]
    B --> C[SSH Server]

docs.title: Topics Covered
docs.text:
• SSH key authentication
  • SSH hardening
  • SCP and SFTP
  • Port forwarding
  • SSH tunnelling
  • Linux administration
  • Troubleshooting

docs.title: Generate SSH Keys
docs.text: ssh-keygen -t ed25519

docs.title: Connect to a Server
docs.text: ssh user@192.168.1.10

docs.title: Example SSH Tunnel
docs.text:
ssh -L 8080:localhost:80 user@server

Warning

Password authentication should be disabled in production environments whenever possible.

docs.title: TLS
docs.text: TLS (Transport Layer Security) secures application traffic over TCP networks and is the foundation of HTTPS and many secure application protocols.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Encryption
  • Authentication
  • Integrity validation
  • Certificate-based trust
  • Perfect Forward Secrecy

docs.title: Common Protocols Using TLS
docs.text: Protocol Usage HTTPS Secure web SMTPS Secure email FTPS Secure file transfer MQTT TLS IoT security

docs.title: TLS Handshake
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Server

    Client->>Server: ClientHello
    Server->>Client: ServerHello + Certificate
    Client->>Server: Key Exchange
    Server->>Client: Secure Session Established

docs.title: Topics Covered
docs.text:
• OpenSSL
  • TLS certificates
  • Certificate Authorities
  • CSR generation
  • Cipher suites
  • TLS debugging
  • HTTPS testing

docs.title: Example OpenSSL Test
docs.text:
openssl s_client -connect google.com:443

Warning

Self-signed certificates are suitable for labs but not production environments.

docs.title: WireGuard
docs.text: WireGuard is a modern Layer 3 VPN protocol focused on simplicity, performance, and cryptographic security.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Minimal configuration
  • High performance
  • Modern cryptography
  • UDP-based transport
  • Simple key management
  • Cross-platform support

docs.title: Cryptography
docs.text: Component Algorithm Key Exchange Curve25519 Encryption ChaCha20 Authentication Poly1305 Hashing BLAKE2s

docs.text:
Site-to-Site VPNRemote AccessLab TopologiesContainer Networking

docs.title: Example Configuration
docs.text:
[Interface]
Address = 10.10.10.1/24
PrivateKey = <private-key>
ListenPort = 51820

[Peer]
PublicKey = <peer-public-key>
AllowedIPs = 10.10.10.2/32
Endpoint = 192.168.1.10:51820

Warning

Incorrect MTU values commonly cause fragmentation and tunnel instability.
